title: Dataset/storage service: unified catalog + access API for all dataset consumers
description:
Datasets are the fundamental unit of mainframe storage interaction, and nearly every jackal component touches them — so dataset interaction should be ONE well-defined service that all consumers use, rather than each utility reaching into catalog internals + importing red-dragon drivers ad hoc. Build this FIRST; every os-runtime dataset feature (GDG, PDS, ESDS/RRDS, AIX, SORT, IEBGENER, IEBCOPY, DCB, concatenation) is a client of it.

CURRENT LEAK (the motivation): DatasetCatalog is the shared *catalog* API (resolve/allocate/dispose/delete_dsn), but (a) the *access* face is not an API — idcams/executor.py imports red-dragon IndexedDriver/SequentialDriver directly and opens them itself, while cobol_step takes catalog.allocate(dd).path and hands a raw Path to red-dragon's RealFileIOProvider (which uses the SAME drivers internally). Two consumers, two ways to reach a dataset's bytes. (b) allocate_ksds bakes one org into the catalog -> would sprawl to allocate_esds/rrds/pds/gdg.

TARGET (two clean faces, mirroring z/OS catalog + DADSM + access methods):
- CATALOG/BINDING face: resolve DSN->Dataset; allocate BY ORG (generalize allocate_ksds -> allocate(spec)); DISP lifecycle; GDG generation resolution; PDS member resolution. The parenthesized qualifier (gen/member) arrives structurally from the JCL grammar (no regex).
- ACCESS face: open-for-read / open-for-write by org -> a record reader/writer, wrapping red-dragon's drivers as the single access API. IDCAMS REPRO, SORT, IEBGENER all read/write through this instead of importing drivers.

CONSUMER-DRIVEN PRINCIPLE (binding instruction): the interfaces must be validated as consumable by EVERY consumer before they are fixed — IDCAMS (binding + access), COBOL steps (binding-ONLY; access is internal to the red-dragon VM via RealFileIOProvider), the runner DD allocate/dispose lifecycle, IEFBR14, and the forward consumers SORT/IEBGENER/IEBCOPY/GDG/PDS/ESDS/RRDS/AIX/DCB/concat. Build a consumer's slice against the API and adjust the API to fit, rather than designing it in isolation.

Constraints: FP/frozen, no None defaults, no defensive guards (fail loud), no regex. Brainstorm -> spec -> plan -> subagent-driven execution. This epic is a sibling to jackal-1o2 (JCL coverage), not a child — its own line of work.
notes:
SUBSTRATE AUDIT (2026-06-25) — design inputs from auditing red-dragon's file drivers + the CobolIOProvider seam:

THE ACCESS-API CONTRACT ALREADY EXISTS: interpreter/cobol/file_drivers.py defines FileOrganizationDriver — a runtime_checkable Protocol with a uniform, OPERATION-COMPLETE method set: open/close/read_seq/read_key/start(browse)/write/rewrite/delete. jackal-vxb's access face should ADOPT/re-export this Protocol as its contract, NOT invent a new one. The 'implicit surface' is FileOrganizationDriver (the Protocol) — NOT RealFileIOProvider (which is merely red-dragon's COBOL *adapter*: it maps VM __cobol_* calls onto a driver; it's the reference shape for jackal's own CobolIOProvider).

DECOUPLING: driver logic is clean (depends only on Path, OpenMode enum, IOResult dataclass; no VM/executor/ASG) and is already used standalone by jackal/idcams/executor.py. ONE WRINKLE: IOResult is defined in io_provider.py, which does 'from interpreter.vm.vm import Operators' — so importing a driver transitively pulls the VM. Benign for jackal (it runs the VM anyway), but the storage substrate is not truly VM-free. If a VM-independent dataset library is ever wanted, IOResult must move to a leaf module. Note for the spec, not a blocker.

COMPLETENESS: operation-complete (full CRUD + sequential + keyed + STARTBR positioning); ORG-partial. Present: PS (SequentialDriver), KSDS (IndexedDriver), RRDS (RelativeDriver — already there, so 1o2.21's RRDS half is substrate-ready; only ESDS is genuinely missing). Missing: ESDS, AIX, PDS members — these are NEW FileOrganizationDriver implementations (or member-routing for PDS) under the SAME Protocol, not a redesign.

IMPLICATION: jackal-vxb is 'consolidate + observe over a solid substrate', NOT 'build a storage engine'. Access face = pick driver by org -> add observability trace -> serve TWO client shapes (a CobolIOProvider adapter for VM-driven COBOL record I/O + status codes; direct Python calls for IDCAMS/SORT/IEBGENER). The CobolIOProvider injection seam (run(io_provider=...)) is how COBOL access plugs in -> COBOL becomes a FULLY-TRACED consumer (not binding-only), the observability-first payoff. Substrate (the 3 drivers) stays red-dragon's; jackal wraps, never reimplements.
RE-SCOPED (2026-06-25): the storage ENGINE (access + neutral outcomes) moved to a red-dragon epic (shared across the mainframe stack — see red-dragon docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-25-shared-access-method-engine-design.md). jackal-vxb is now JUST the jackal dataset CATALOG (DSN->dataset, DISP lifecycle, GDG generations, PDS members) that CONSUMES the red-dragon engine + maps neutral outcomes -> COBOL FILE STATUS. Observability/tracing deferred. This becomes actionable only after the red-dragon engine's first piece lands and is bumped in.
close_reason: DatasetSpec + allocate_new + open_dataset implemented; allocate_ksds deleted; executor wired through catalog; ValueError→MAXCC=12 fix included. 77 tests green.

title: JCL parser via ANTLR grammar behind a Java bridge (proleap-bridge pattern); retire Lark
description: Foundation for thorough JCL coverage. ARCHITECTURE (decided): adopt a mature ANTLR4 JCL grammar in JAVA and call it from Python through a bridge, exactly like red-dragon's proleap-bridge does for COBOL — NOT a pure-Python ANTLR target. The bridge parses JCL (Java/ANTLR) and serializes a structured AST (JSON) back to Python; jackal deserializes into its EXISTING frozen model (Job/Step/DD/Disp). The hand-written Lark grammar (jackal/jcl/grammar.lark + Transformer) is retired. Candidate grammar: cschneid-the-elder/mapa (MIT) — bridge route means its embedded Java actions + symbolic-substitution + disposition analysis are REUSED, not stripped (the key advantage over pure-Python generation). Tasks: (1) spike — confirm mapa's JCL .g4 parses the real CardDemo jobs in Java; (2) stand up the bridge (extend proleap-bridge or a sibling jcl-bridge JAR; a JclSerializer -> JSON like StatementSerializer/AsgSerializer); (3) Python side calls the bridge via RealSubprocessRunner + bridge JAR (build product, like proleap), deserializes to the model; (4) migrate v2 features (in-stream, SYSOUT) + delete Lark; (5) re-green full suite + gated CardDemo e2e. RUNTIME: JVM per parse (already paid for COBOL). Attribution: keep upstream LICENSE/provenance.
design: Open design forks for the spec: (a) extend the EXISTING proleap-bridge JAR vs a SEPARATE jcl-bridge JAR; (b) mapa vs grossvater/jcl-parser as the grammar; (c) serialization contract (JSON shape) JCL-bridge -> Python. Must reproduce 100% of current Lark parse behavior (incl. in-stream/SYSOUT/the e2e jobs) before merge. Spike de-risks (a)/(b) before committing.
notes: SPIKE RESULT (2026-06-21): GO — grammar = cschneid-the-elder/mapa, MIT. JCL grammar at mapa/jcl/src/JCLParser.g4 (1002L) + JCLLexer.g4 (5096L), start rule 'startRule', tokenVocab=JCLLexer. ACTION-FREE (2 lexer-mode brace sites only) -> clean for a thin Java bridge. Coverage present: JOB/EXEC(PGM=/PROC=)/DD + per-param rules (DISP/DSN/SPACE/SYSOUT/UNIT/VOLUME/COND), in-stream (DD */DATA/DLM, grammar-native), DD concatenation, COND=, IF/ELSE/ENDIF, PROC/PEND + symbolics, GDG gen refs, referbacks (DSN=*.STEP.DD), JOBLIB/SYSCHK, OUTPUT, SET, INCLUDE, EXPORT. EVIDENCE: 38/38 CardDemo .jcl parse with ZERO errors via antlr4-parse (ANTLR 4.13.1); error detection verified on garbage. Column sensitivity (cols 73-80, // markers) handled INSIDE the lexer -> no 80-col pre-splitting needed. In-stream/SYSIN grammar-native -> no manual extraction. Separate JCLPP preprocessor grammar exists for symbolic/INCLUDE expansion — DESIGN FORK: parse raw structure (sufficient now; 38/38 was raw) vs run JCLPP first (needed for PROC/symbolics, 1o2.2). grossvater/jcl-parser REJECTED: Apache-2.0 but action-heavy, needs custom Java lexer, semantically weak (opaque FIELD_ID/params, no DISP/COND/GDG rules). Java glue needed: small — a main that runs lexer+parser and serializes the tree to JSON on stdout (proleap-bridge shape).
close_reason: Merged to main (9a7ec7d). JCL parsed via mapa ANTLR grammar behind jcl-bridge Java bridge; Lark retired; 42 tests green incl gated CardDemo e2e + parse-sweep (TRANBKP/DEFGDGB now parse). Malformed-JSON->JclParseError. Carried follow-ups (non-blocking): PROC= parsing untested (1o2.2), no Java unit test.

title: Generation Data Groups (GDG): relative + absolute generation refs
description: GDGs (DSN=A.B.C(+1), (0), (-1)) are pervasive for dated/cyclic batch datasets. Add a GDG base + generation model to the catalog: define a GDG base (IDCAMS DEFINE GDG or pre-seeded), resolve (+1)=new generation, (0)=current, (-n)=nth prior; roll generations on job completion per DISP. Without this, jobs referencing generation datasets fail to resolve DSNs.
design: Catalog gains a GDG registry mapping base -> ordered generation list; DSN resolution interprets the (gen) suffix at allocate time; (+1) allocations are cataloged on step/job success per normal disposition. Parse the (gen) suffix in the DSN grammar token, not regex.

title: Step-level conditional execution: COND= (RC-gated step bypass)
description: Steps currently always run regardless of prior return codes. Add JCL-level COND= on EXEC cards (and job-level COND=) to bypass steps based on prior step return codes: COND=(code,op[,stepname]) — bypass this step if 'code op RC' is true (operands reversed); multiple conditions COND=((c,op),(c,op)) bypass if ANY is true. CardDemo uses (0,NE) ('skip if any prior step failed') and (4,LT) pervasively. RC-only scope: no COND=EVEN/ONLY, no JCL IF/THEN/ENDIF (those are split to a sibling issue; IDCAMS-level IF/THEN already works). Runner gains per-step RC state; bypassed steps -> StepResult(ran=False).
design: Grammar: extend exec_card for COND=; add if_stmt/else/endif statements at the job level (Lark, no regex). Runner: maintain a step-RC map; evaluate conditions before dispatch; mark skipped steps in JobResult (ran=False, distinct from RC). COND= semantics are inverted ('bypass if true') — document carefully. IF/THEN is the modern, clearer form; COND= the legacy form — support both.
notes: ARCH-REVIEW CROSS-REF (2026-06-22): the whole-branch review of 1o2.9 independently flagged the same root issue this covers — cobol_step.py hardcodes StepResult return_code=0 (cobol_step.py:66), the runner never checks step RCs so a job never aborts on failure, and Disp.abnormal is modelled but dead (never consulted by catalog.dispose). All resolved by this issue's plan: wire real RETURN-CODE via read_return_code(vm), thread RC into step sequencing, and (for abnormal disp) branch dispose on step success/failure. The StepResult.ran->StepDisposition enum chosen here also addresses the review's boolean-blindness note.
close_reason: Merged to main. COND= conditional step execution: real COBOL RETURN-CODE (Part 1), Cond/CondOp model + StepDisposition, pure should_bypass (IBM reversed operands), bridge emits cond (execParmCOND/jobParmCOND), runner fold bypasses steps. 7 tasks subagent-driven, final review Ready-to-merge, full suite 71 green incl real-COBOL COND e2e. EVEN/ONLY+IF/THEN fail loud -> deferred to 1o2.8. Follow-up: jackal-449 (condFromWords silent catch).

title: Broaden jackal JCL execution coverage beyond the v2 vertical slice
description: jackal v2 proved one deep vertical slice (IDCAMS provision/load -> COBOL read, byte-faithful EBCDIC, real CardDemo ACCTFILE->READACCT). This epic broadens coverage toward 'understand/execute useful JCL'. STRATEGY CHANGE: rather than grow the hand-written Lark grammar feature-by-feature, ADOPT a mature reference ANTLR4 JCL grammar (candidate: cschneid-the-elder/mapa, MIT — already does symbolic substitution + dataset disposition) and GENERATE A PURE-PYTHON PARSER from it (ANTLR Python3 target: Java at build time, antlr4-python3-runtime at runtime; no JVM per parse). This makes thorough PARSING a one-shot foundation; the remaining gap sub-projects then become EXECUTION-semantics work layered on the parsed model. Tier model: Tier0 skeleton (DONE), Tier1 execution-shaping JCL (COND/IF, PROC/symbolics, GDG, DD concatenation, referbacks, && temp, DCB), Tier2 utility control-languages (IDCAMS partial, SORT, IEBGENER — each its own embedded language), Tier3 operational tail (mostly skip). Re-prioritized by REAL CardDemo leverage: GDG(14 jobs) > COND(5) > SORT/IEBGENER(4) > IDCAMS-depth(61 steps); PROC dropped to P3 (0 CardDemo jobs use cataloged/instream PROCs).
design: Priority order reflects what blocks running MORE real jobs: (1) step-level control flow (COND/IF) — jobs branch on RC; (2) PROC + symbolic params — most real JCL is unparseable without them; (3) SORT/IEBGENER — every batch chain sorts/copies; then GDG, DD concatenation, IDCAMS breadth, SYSOUT capture. Each child should preserve the v2 binding constraints: Lark grammars (no regex), FP/frozen dataclasses, no None defaults, no silent guards, TDD, gated real-checkout e2e where applicable.
notes: PARSING SUBSUMPTION (post-spike): 1o2.9 adopts the mapa ANTLR grammar which already PARSES COND/IF/PROC/symbolics/GDG/concatenation/referbacks/DCB/PARM/DUMMY/INCLUDE/in-stream (38/38 CardDemo clean). So every feature sub-issue below becomes EXECUTION-SEMANTICS ONLY once 1o2.9 lands — the 'parse X' half is free. Sequence 1o2.9 first.

title: PDS/PDSE partitioned datasets + member access (DSN=LIB(MEMBER))
description: BIGGEST structural gap surfaced by the roadmap map. A jackal dataset is a single file with no member concept; real jobs reference DSN=SOME.LIB(MEMBER) pervasively. Add a partitioned-dataset model (a directory of members) + member resolution in the catalog/DD layer. Underpins: STEPLIB/JOBLIB load-library member resolution (programs loaded from a lib, not just source_dir), library-based PROC/INCLUDE/copybook/SORT-control lookup, and IEBCOPY. Prerequisite for shop-standard (Class D) jobs. Likely a small sub-epic.
design: Model: a PDS Dataset whose backing path is a directory; members are files inside; DSN(MEMBER) resolves to <dir>/<MEMBER>. DD without member = whole PDS (concatenation/IEBCOPY); with member = that file. Threads into allocate/resolve and the COBOL/utility provider. Interacts with DD concatenation (1o2.5) for STEPLIB chains and PROC libs (1o2.2/1o2.15).

title: PARM= — pass parameters into the executed program
description: 4 CardDemo jobs pass PARM= on EXEC. A program receives PARM via its entry linkage (COBOL: PROCEDURE DIVISION USING / the JCL parm area). Execution: thread the parsed PARM string into the red-dragon run() so the COBOL program sees its startup argument. Parsing from 1o2.9.

title: Honor DCB attributes (LRECL/RECFM/BLKSIZE) in allocation + record I/O
description: 13 CardDemo jobs specify DCB=/RECFM/LRECL. Record length + format drive file I/O (fixed vs variable records, blocking). Execution: thread DCB attrs from the parsed DD into dataset allocation and into the record codec red-dragon uses, so reads/writes use the declared LRECL/RECFM instead of assumptions. Subsumes/【generalizes the v2 debt item jackal-ifq (REPRO LRECL assumption). Parsing comes from the adopted grammar (1o2.9).

title: Temporary datasets (&&NAME): job-scoped scratch files
description: &&NAME denotes a temporary dataset that lives for the job and is auto-deleted at job end. Common Tier-1 JCL (passed between steps). Execution = catalog allocates a workdir-scoped temp file keyed by &&name, visible across steps, disposed at job end.
close_reason: &&NAME temporary dataset lifecycle implemented: DirectDSN/TempRef type hierarchy, bridge parser TempRef emission, catalog temp registry with allocate/dispose/cleanup_temps, try/finally exception-safe cleanup in runner. 5 integration tests + 8 unit tests. All 111 tests pass.

title: Backward references: DSN=*.STEP.DD (and *.STEP.PROCSTEP.DD)
description: Resolve a DD's dataset by referring back to a prior step's DD (DSN=*.STEP.DDNAME). Common Tier-1 JCL. Parsing comes from the adopted grammar; execution = catalog resolves the referenced step/DD's dataset at allocate time. Requires the runner to expose prior steps' resolved DDs.
close_reason: DSN=*.STEP.DD backward reference resolution implemented: BackwardRef type, Java bridge backref JSON emission, Python parser dispatch, runner _resolve_step/_record_dds with IBM bypass propagation. 5 unit + 2 integration tests. 123 tests pass.

title: Broaden IDCAMS verb coverage (LISTCAT, PRINT, alternate indexes, REPRO variants)
description: v2 IDCAMS supports only DELETE CLUSTER / DEFINE CLUSTER / REPRO INFILE-OUTFILE / IF-MAXCC. Real IDCAMS jobs also use: LISTCAT (catalog listing), PRINT (dump records), DEFINE AIX + BLDINDEX (alternate indexes), REPRO with FROMKEY/TOKEY/COUNT/SKIP, DELETE of non-cluster entries, ALTER. Extend the IDCAMS grammar+executor incrementally as real jobs demand them; each unknown verb currently fails loud (good).
design: Additive to jackal/idcams/grammar.lark + executor.py. Prioritize by what the CardDemo batch chain actually uses (audit its IDCAMS steps first). Keep fail-loud for still-unsupported verbs.

title: DD concatenation (multiple datasets under one DDname)
description: Concatenated DDs (a //DD with DSN, followed by // DD cards with no ddname) present multiple datasets to a program as one logical sequential stream — common for STEPLIB/JOBLIB and multi-file input. Add: grammar for the unnamed-continuation DD form; model a DD as carrying an ordered list of datasets; sequential reads span the concatenation in order.
design: Grammar: a dd_card with an empty NAME position concatenates onto the preceding DD. Model: DD.datasets: tuple[...] (or a Concatenation wrapper) — preserve frozen/FP. red-dragon SequentialDriver reads must chain across members (or jackal concatenates at provide time). Interacts with STEPLIB once PROC/load-lib semantics land.

title: SORT and IEBGENER utilities
description: Every batch chain sorts and copies. Add two utilities to the registry: SORT (DFSORT/SyncSort — SORT FIELDS=, INCLUDE/OMIT, SUM, OUTREC/INREC reformatting via SYSIN control statements; SORTIN->SORTOUT) and IEBGENER (sequential copy SYSUT1->SYSUT2, optional record reformatting). Both read control statements from SYSIN in-stream (already supported). Start with the common subset (SORT FIELDS + basic INCLUDE/OMIT; IEBGENER straight copy).
design: New jackal/sort/ + jackal/iebgener/ (or a shared utility module) with Lark grammars for the control languages, mirroring jackal/idcams/. SORT FIELDS=(start,len,format,order) operate on byte-faithful EBCDIC records via red-dragon drivers. MAXCC/RC mapping like IDCAMS. Scope the SORT control-statement subset explicitly.

title: Backward references: *.STEP.PROCSTEP.DD (PROC-nested form)
description: Support DSN=*.STEP.PROCSTEP.DD backward references — the three-segment form used when the referenced DD is inside a cataloged or instream PROC. Deferred from jackal-1o2.10 (which covers the two-segment *.STEP.DD form only) until PROC support (jackal-1o2.2) lands, since the PROCSTEP segment is meaningless without PROC execution.

title: Guard against &&NAME / DirectDSN backing-file collision in catalog
description: TempRef('&&FOO') and DirectDSN('FOO') both resolve to workdir/'FOO'. If a job allocates both, the second write truncates the first silently. Add a test and a guard (e.g. check for path collision on allocation, or prefix temp backing files with a sentinel).

title: Eliminate double-parse when PARM is set in cobol_step (merge _file_control into compile_cobol)
description: When step.parm is non-empty, cobol_step.py calls both _file_control() (ProLeap Java bridge subprocess) and compile_cobol() separately — parsing the COBOL source twice and paying two JVM startup costs. _file_control only needs the file_control list from the ProLeap parse result, which compile_cobol already produces internally. Merge the two calls into one.

title: Expose stable cobol_entry_point() helper in red-dragon to avoid func_init_params_ prefix coupling
description: cobol_step.py scans func_symbol_table for non-func_init_params_ labels to find the COBOL program entry point (mirroring run() internals). This couples jackal to red-dragon's internal naming convention. red-dragon should expose a stable API like cobol_entry_point(linked: LinkedProgram) -> EntryPoint that encapsulates this logic.

title: PARM e2e via real CBACT04C/INTCALC (deferred — needs batch AIX PATH)
description: Once batch alternate-index PATH access (jackal-1o2.22) lands, add a real INTCALC.jcl / CBACT04C e2e that asserts PARM='2022071800' (passed via PARM=, jackal-1o2.13) reaches PARM-DATE and appears in the written TRANFILE transaction record (CBACT04C 1300-B-WRITE-TX: STRING PARM-DATE ... WRITE FD-TRANFILE-REC). Currently blocked: CBACT04C needs 5 VSAM files incl. XREFFIL1=CARDXREF.VSAM.AIX.PATH (an alternate-index PATH), which batch jackal does not support yet. PARM faithfulness itself is validated now by a minimal purpose-built EXTERNAL-PARMS program (jackal-1o2.13); this is the fuller real-job witness. Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-26-parm-linkage-design.md.

title: make jar does not rebuild when only Java sources change (stale-JAR footgun)
description: The Makefile 'jar' target gates on the JAR FILE existing ($(JCL_BRIDGE_JAR): with no source prerequisites), so after editing a .java the mtime check sees the JAR present and prints 'Nothing to be done for jar' — silently testing against a STALE JAR. Hit live during jackal-449: tests passed against the old JAR until a forced 'mvn package' rebuilt it. 'make jar-force' works but is easy to forget; 'make test' depends on 'jar' so it inherits the staleness. Fix options: (a) make $(JCL_BRIDGE_JAR) depend on its .java/.g4/pom sources (find jcl-bridge/src -newer); (b) make 'jar' always run mvn (mvn is incremental anyway); (c) document jar-force after Java edits. Same pattern in cicada/squall Makefiles (proleap bridge) — fix consistently. Build-correctness issue: a green suite could be validating stale Java.

title: RESTART= — resume a job at a named step/procstep
description: JCL-language execution semantics. RESTART=stepname (or stepname.procstep) on the JOB card makes execution begin at that step rather than the first, skipping all prior steps (used for rerunning a failed job from the point of failure). 1 CardDemo job uses it. Execution: the runner skips steps until the named one, then runs normally; skipped steps -> StepResult(disposition=BYPASSED/SKIPPED, like COND). Parsing comes from the adopted ANTLR grammar (1o2.9). Pure JCL-language feature (no OS/utility dependency).
design: Pairs with the StepDisposition enum from 1o2.1. Interacts with referbacks (1o2.10) — a RESTART that skips the step a later DSN=*.step.dd refers back to must error clearly. Job-card param.

title: Abend model: program abends (Sxxx/Uxxx) distinct from return codes
description: Failures are RC-shaped today; real programs ABEND (S0C7 data exception, U-user abends) which is distinct from a clean nonzero RC and flushes the rest of the job unless COND=EVEN/ONLY. Needed for realistic failure semantics + EVEN/ONLY (jackal-1o2.8) + dump DDs. Model an abend outcome on StepResult (alongside the StepDisposition enum from 1o2.1) and have run_job stop subsequent steps on abend.

title: IEBCOPY utility — copy/compress PDS members
description: Common library utility: copy members between PDSes, compress, selective COPY/EXCLUDE via SYSIN. Depends on PDS member support (jackal-1o2.16). New jackal/iebcopy/ grammar+executor in the IDCAMS shape; register in UTILITIES.

title: Load-library resolution: find programs via STEPLIB/JOBLIB PDS members
description: Today jackal resolves a program by name from source_dir (<pgm>.cbl). Real jobs locate the load module as a member of a STEPLIB/JOBLIB library (often concatenated). Once PDS members exist (depends on jackal-1o2.16), resolve EXEC PGM=X by searching the STEPLIB/JOBLIB member chain before falling back to source_dir. Removes the OPTIONAL_DDS STEPLIB-skip workaround in cobol_step.py.

title: INCLUDE / JCLLIB expansion (execution)
description: 3 CardDemo jobs use INCLUDE/JCLLIB (splice a shared JCL fragment from a library). Execution: resolve the INCLUDE member from a configured library dir and splice its statements before sequencing. mapa's grammar parses INCLUDE; its JCLPP preprocessor may do expansion (see 1o2.9 raw-vs-preprocess fork). Parsing from 1o2.9.

title: DUMMY / DSN=NULLFILE DDs (empty input / discard output)
description: 4 CardDemo jobs use DUMMY/NULLFILE DDs — a read returns EOF immediately, a write is discarded. Execution: catalog/provider resolves a DUMMY DD to an empty-source / sink dataset. Parsing from 1o2.9.

title: JCL-level IF/THEN/ELSE/ENDIF + COND=EVEN/ONLY (abend-conditional execution)
description: Split from jackal-1o2.1. The modern JCL conditional construct (// IF (cond) THEN ... // ELSE ... // ENDIF) and the abend-conditional COND=EVEN/ONLY forms. NOT used by CardDemo (its IF/THEN are all IDCAMS SYSIN, already handled; no EVEN/ONLY present), so deferred. IF/THEN/ENDIF reintroduces nesting into the flat Job.steps model + runner (needs a job-item tree or block construct) and abend modeling (jackal has no abend concept yet — failures are currently RC-shaped). Design when a real job needs it.

title: REPRO assumes PS LRECL == KSDS record_size
description: jackal/idcams/executor.py REPRO uses the OUTFILE KSDS record_size for BOTH the SequentialDriver (INFILE/PS) and IndexedDriver (OUTFILE/KSDS). Correct when PS LRECL == KSDS RECORDSIZE (the v2 case, 300), but a PS with a different LRECL would be mis-blocked. Source the input record length from the PS dataset/its DD, not the output KSDS.

title: Capture and surface SYSOUT output
description: SYSOUT=* DDs are parsed but their output is discarded. Programs/utilities write messages, reports, and control-statement echoes to SYSOUT; for real-job fidelity and debugging, capture per-step SYSOUT and surface it (in JobResult/StepResult, optionally to files in the workdir). IDCAMS especially echoes its control statements + condition codes to SYSPRINT.
design: Route SYSOUT/SYSPRINT writes to an in-memory buffer per step, expose on StepResult (e.g. sysout: tuple[str,...]); optionally persist to workdir. Utilities (IDCAMS/SORT) should emit their standard message lines + final condition code. Keep StepResult frozen.

title: PROC support + symbolic parameters (&VAR, cataloged + instream PROCs)
description: Most production JCL invokes cataloged procedures (//STEP EXEC PROCNAME) and parameterizes via symbolics (&VAR=val, defaulted in PROC, overridden on EXEC). Without this, the majority of real JCL cannot even be PARSED, let alone run. Add: instream PROC (//name PROC ... //  PEND), cataloged PROC resolution from a proclib search path, symbolic parameter substitution (definition, defaulting, EXEC-level override), and PROC step DD overrides/additions (//STEP.DD).
design: Symbolic substitution must NOT be a regex pass over text (violates the no-regex constraint) — model symbolics as grammar tokens and resolve during/after parse into the Step/DD model. PROC expansion = splice resolved PROC steps into the job step list with symbolic bindings applied. Needs a proclib dir CLI flag (mirror --source-dir/--copybook-dir). This is the largest single task; may warrant its own sub-epic.
notes: SCOPE (2026-06-24): include the JCL SET statement (// SET VAR=val) here — it is the symbolic-assignment half of the substitution layer (defines/overrides symbols for subsequent &VAR references). 1 CardDemo job uses SET. Belongs with PROC/symbolic-parameter handling, not a separate issue.

title: jcl-bridge: condFromWords silently catches NumberFormatException -> code=0
description: Code-quality follow-up from the COND= (jackal-1o2.1) final review. JclSerializer.condFromWords wraps Integer.parseInt of the COND code slot in try{}catch(NumberFormatException){/* 0 */}, silently defaulting a non-numeric code to 0. Unreachable for valid JCL (the mapa number token guarantees numeric), and the Python op-validation still fails loud for EVEN/ONLY — so it cannot mask a bypass decision — but it violates the letter of the no-silent-guard constraint. Fix: remove the catch (let it parse) or assert it cannot happen. Trivial.
close_reason: Fixed (merged to main, 7d640ed): condFromWords parses the COND code slot directly; removed the swallowed NumberFormatException->0. Fails loud on a malformed code; EVEN/ONLY unaffected (handled separately). 4 COND bridge tests + full suite green against the rebuilt JAR.

title: OUTPUT JCL statement — JES spool output descriptors
description: JCL-language construct: the //name OUTPUT statement defines a spool/print output descriptor (CLASS, DEST, FORMS, etc.) that SYSOUT DDs reference via OUTPUT=. 3 CardDemo jobs use it. Almost entirely operational (print routing) with no batch-execution effect in an emulator. Execution: parse-and-ignore (record the descriptor, don't act on it) is sufficient; surface it only if/when SYSOUT capture (1o2.7) wants the CLASS/DEST. Low priority; mainly here so it is parsed-and-modeled, not a gap that breaks a job.

title: TYPRUN= (SCAN / HOLD) — parse-only and hold execution modes
description: JCL-language execution semantics. TYPRUN=SCAN means 'syntax-check the JCL only, do not execute any step' (a dry-run mode); TYPRUN=HOLD means 'queue but do not run until released'. 0 CardDemo jobs use it, but it is a real JCL-language execution mode. Execution: SCAN -> parse + validate, return a JobResult with all steps disposition=NOT-RUN and RC 0, run nothing; HOLD -> in a non-interactive runner, treat as a no-op/immediate-release (or a clear 'held' status). Parsing from 1o2.9. JOB-card param.

title: Deeper DFSORT (INREC/OUTREC/JOINKEYS) + ICETOOL
description: Beyond the SORT subset in jackal-1o2.3 (FIELDS/INCLUDE/OMIT/SUM): record reformatting (INREC/OUTREC), multi-file joins (JOINKEYS), and the ICETOOL report/stats toolkit. Large surface — scope incrementally as real jobs demand. Extends jackal-1o2.3.

title: JCL system symbols (&SYSUID, &SYSDATE, &SYSTIME, JES symbols)
description: System-defined symbolic substitutions (distinct from PROC symbolics) used in DSNs/dates/generated names. Resolve during/after parse; shares the substitution machinery with PROC symbolics (jackal-1o2.2).

title: VSAM alternate indexes (DEFINE AIX + BLDINDEX, PATH access)
description: Secondary-key access over a base KSDS: IDCAMS DEFINE AIX + BLDINDEX builds the index; programs open the PATH. Extends IDCAMS depth (jackal-1o2.6) + the VSAM model.

title: VSAM ESDS / RRDS access methods
description: Entry-sequenced (ESDS) and relative-record (RRDS) VSAM datasets, beyond the KSDS already supported. Catalog DatasetOrg + red-dragon driver wiring; IDCAMS DEFINE for the new org types. Narrower than KSDS but blocks specific real jobs.

title: Diagnostic DDs: SYSUDUMP / CEEDUMP / SYSABEND capture
description: Abend dump DDs programs declare for diagnostics. Start as capture-and-route-to-sysout (or workdir file); meaningful content depends on the abend model. Pairs with SYSOUT capture (1o2.7) and the abend model.

title: e2e step-name list assertion is brittle
description: tests/integration/test_carddemo_acctfile_e2e.py asserts the exact step-name list ['STEP05','STEP10','STEP15']. Non-vacuous but tied to the shipped JCL; would give a confusing failure if the JCL is restructured. Consider asserting per-step RC keyed by name, or relaxing to count+presence.
